text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Christian Democrats try to secure vote of no confidence in Social Democrat state government of Saxony-Anhalt to clarify role of reform communists
- German President Herzog begins visit to China
- Deutsche Telekom shares climb strongly
- Finance ministry expects net new public sector borrowing to be about 99 billion marks in 1997
HANDELSBLATT
- Deutsche Telekom shares open far above issue price
- Liberal Free Democrats insist that income tax surcharge will fall in 1998
- Jobs continue to be cut in engineering sector, albeit slowly
- Viag's Schmalbach-Lubeca to cooperate with Pechiney
- One-third of west German engineering firms making loss, Ifo institute survey shows
- Waigel says EMU stability pact may be postponed until 1997
- West German pensions to rise 1.7 percent in 1997
- Plastics manufacturers to control recycling in future
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- NATO agrees to send new peacekeeping mission to Bosnia
- German President Herzog plans "frank talks" in China
- Deutsche Telekom shares fulfil expectations, rise after listing
- Pensions to rise more than expected in 1997
- Bundesbank director Welteke expects "quiet" Bundesbank meeting
- Compuserve considers moving out of Germany should legal environment for Internet become more difficult
- One-third of west German engineering firms making loss, Ifo institute survey shows
DIE WELT
- Bonn fearful for its nationals in Iran because of terrorism trial in Berlin
- Deutsche Telekom shares make strong start on Frankfurt bourse, traders warn against quick sale
- Banks try to make use of rush of investors for client counselling
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
